name: packetstream
description: Live web search results and web pages as Markdown for Codex, from PacketStream's hosted MCP server.

interface.longDescription:
PacketStream gives ChatGPT and Codex two read-only tools. packetstream_search runs a live search on the world's most-used search engine and returns the results as Markdown and JSON. It can target a country, a language or a city, and it covers web, news, shopping, places, autocomplete, scholarly and AI answer results. packetstream_fetch reads the page at a URL and returns it as Markdown, not a summary, fetched through PacketStream's residential network. This helps when direct requests are blocked or get CAPTCHAs.

You sign in with your PacketStream account when you connect. Each successful call costs $0.0025 from your prepaid balance, and failed calls are free. PacketStream has no free tier: you add funds first, with a $50 minimum purchase.

Limits: fetch reads static HTML only, so a page that needs JavaScript returns an error. Fetch does not read robots.txt; you decide which sites to read. Page text is returned as untrusted data.
defaultPrompt: Search the news for this week's interest rate decisions and summarize them.
Find the top 3 coffee shops in Austin, Texas and read their websites.
Read https://packetstream.io/docs/mcp/ and list the two tools it describes.

positive.prompt: What has the European Central Bank announced in the past week? Give me the main headlines with links.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls packetstream_search with type news (news takes only country, language and page), then lists recent headlines with their source links. It does not invent stories that are not in the results.

positive.description: Search targeted to a country and language
positive.prompt: Search the web as someone in Germany, in German, for "beste Laufschuhe" and list the top five results.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls packetstream_search with query "beste Laufschuhe", country de and language de, then lists five results with titles and links, as the German results page shows them.

positive.prompt: Find three well-rated bakeries in Austin, Texas, with their addresses.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls packetstream_search with type places and a query that names the city, such as "bakeries in Austin, Texas" (places takes only country and language), then names three bakeries with the addresses and ratings from the results.

positive.description: Read a page the user gives
positive.prompt: Read https://packetstream.io/docs/mcp/ and tell me what the two tools do and what a call costs.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls packetstream_fetch with that URL, then says that packetstream_search runs a live web search and packetstream_fetch reads a page as Markdown, and that each successful call costs $0.0025.

positive.prompt: Find the official Model Context Protocol specification, open it, and tell me the latest protocol version it lists.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls packetstream_search to find modelcontextprotocol.io, then packetstream_fetch on the specification page, and reports the version string shown on that page, citing the URL.

negative.prompt: Write a Python function that checks whether a string is a palindrome.
Post a comment saying "Great article!" on https://example.com/blog/post-1.
Log in to my online bank and download last month's statement.

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing in the chat. Tool calls are billed to the user's existing prepaid PacketStream balance.

publication.release_notes: First release: packetstream_search and packetstream_fetch on PacketStream's hosted MCP server (server version 1.5.0), with sign-in on /v1/mcp/oauth.
